title: Introduce policy simulator with KMS proofing and audit-diff tooling
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds a dry-run policy simulator for RBAC v2 policies with optional signed KMS proofs for simulated decisions, plus an audit-diff report generator for compliance reviews.
description: Title: Introduce policy simulator with KMS proofing and audit-diff tooling. Motivation: Customers and internal auditors frequently ask for a way to validate RBAC v2 policy changes before rollout and to produce cryptographic proof that a proposed change does not widen region/KMS residency exposure. This PR adds a developer-facing simulator (rbac-sim) that evaluates a set of example requests against a candidate policy delta, emits a human- and machine-readable audit-diff, and (optionally) attaches a short-lived KMS-signed proof bundle that attests to the simulator inputs and outputs for downstream compliance workflows. This is intended to reduce post-deploy surprises, speed review cycles for Dedicated/Private deployments, and plug into our audit retention processes. Summary of changes (high level commits): 1) feat(simulator): introduce rbac-sim CLI and library with JSON policy delta apply and evaluation harness — high-level API, test suite and example fixtures (commit 1/6). 2) feat(audit-diff): add audit-diff generator that produces compact ndjson with decision-level deltas and counts for each service/operation combination (commit 2/6). 3) feat(kms-proof): add optional KMS proof signer that wraps the simulator run in a signed envelope (supporting both hosted KMS and customer CMKs via delegation tokens) (commit 3/6). 4) chore(ci): add unit and integration tests to workflow and container build step (commit 4/6). 5) docs: add quickstart and compliance playbook describing how to run sims against production policy snapshots and how to consume proof bundles (commit 5/6). 6) perf: small perf improvement to policy compile cache to keep simulator runs under 300ms for typical policy sets (commit 6/6). Changed areas/files (high level): - services/rbac/simulator/{main.go,simulator.go,policy_parser.go,fixtures/} - tools/rbac-sim/dockerfile and Makefile - libs/kms/proof_signer.go with integrations for hosted KMS and delegated CMK tokens - infra/ci/rbac-sim.yml (unit + policy integration tests) - docs/compliance/rbac-simulator.md and examples/compliance/playbook.md - testdata/policy-deltas/* (example deltas used in CI) Review notes and design decisions: - Simulator semantics intentionally mirror production PDP evaluation order; we reuse policy compile and the PDP cache. Edge cases for resource wildcards were clarified and documented. - KMS proofing is opt-in; the envelope contains a compact SHA256 of the input fixtures and the ndjson audit-diff, a timestamp, and a signer id. Proofs use existing hosted KMS signing key by default; for Dedicated/Private customers we accept a delegated CMK token and include the key fingerprint in the envelope metadata. - We modeled the audit-diff format around existing ndjson conventions used by the observability team so the output can be ingested into our log-retention and compliance pipelines without extra transformation. - Security review: ephemeral tokens for delegated CMK usage are validated against operator-scoped grants; we added additional guardrails to prevent simulator-initiated KMS requests from being used as an escalation vector. Testing and CI: - Unit tests added for policy parser edge cases, comparator and ndjson generation. - Integration test runs in CI spin up a minimal policy store and runs three representative deltas; artifacts are validated (ndjson schema + optional proof envelope signature verification). - CI checks passed on final run: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass), lint (pass). Review conversation (condensed into single timeline): - Ethan Chu (reviewer): "Nice to see a simulator — two asks: 1) make sure the simulator cannot call production KMS by default; 2) add a gated flag for proofing so that automated CI jobs don't accidentally sign artifacts with hosted keys." - Author (Priya): "Both addressed — default is dry-run-only and proofing requires explicit --enable-proof + env var pointing to KMS key alias. Added tests to assert the default behavior." - Marisol Vega (reviewer): "We should include a short retention policy recommendation for proof bundles — added a doc comment." - Samir Patel (security reviewer): "Verified token validation logic and put a small nit on log noise; asked for an additional audit check that the simulator writes a non-replayable nonce into the envelope." - Priya: "Added nonce and updated docs; also added an integration test that verifies nondeterminism across runs with the same inputs when nonce is present." - Merge readiness: reviewers approved after two rounds of fixes. CI green on approval. Observability and ops notes: - Simulator runs emit metrics under rbac.simulator.run.{success,failure,duration_ms} and proofing emits rbac.simulator.proof.sign.{success,failure}. - Console: added a minimal dashboard tile for recent simulator runs (docs include Grafana snippet). - Rollout plan: feature behind a feature flag rbac.simulator.enabled; default disabled in Hosted. Admins can enable per-tenant for Dedicated and Private installs. Compliance playbook: - How to run: ./tools/rbac-sim --policy-snapshot /path/to/snapshot --delta /path/to/delta.json --out audit-diff.ndjson --enable-proof --kms-key=alias/custom-cmk - How to review: the audit-diff groups changed allow/deny decisions by service and includes sample example requests that would change decision. Proof bundle contains base64(signed_envelope)+ndjson and a verification helper script for auditors. Migration and operational impact: - No runtime changes to PDP; simulator is a standalone tool and library. - Policy changes should still go through standard Linear flow; engineers are encouraged to attach audit-diff + proof to policy change PRs. - For Dedicated/Private customers, operator docs include steps to provide CMK delegation tokens and to configure short-term key usage. Security mitigations implemented: - Simulator KMS operations are rate-limited and annotated; we added a sandbox KMS path for Hosted to avoid accidental use of production keys in automated workflows. - Proof envelopes include signer id, key fingerprint, timestamp, nonce and a tight TTL (default 24h). - Added RBAC rule to prevent non-admin roles from creating proof-enabled simulator runs through the API wrapper. Known limitations and future work: - Current simulator validates policy deltas only; future work will support side-by-side multi-tenant scenarios where composite policy resolution is necessary. - We do not yet automatically attach simulator artifacts to Linear tickets; that will be a small follow-up (ENG-4369). Merge outcome: merged via squash/merge after approvals; release note drafted and added to changelog. Additional metadata: example command lines, proof envelope format and verification helper included in docs. Contact: priya@redwood.example for follow-ups.
